transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood Solutions), Sarah Patel (Nimbus - Head ML Infra), James Lee (Nimbus - Principal ML Eng), Amir Khan (Nimbus - SRE)

Summary: Scoped benchmark integration: customer scripts, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming tests, and pilot timeline.

[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intros, I'm Olivia, AE at Redwood. Marco's our SE, Nina's on solutions. Sarah?
[00:06] Sarah Patel: Hi, Sarah here, head of ML infra at Nimbus, and James and Amir with me. Thanks for the time.
[00:11] Marco Ruiz: Hi all. Quick agenda - figure out what scripts you want us to run, the target SLAs, and then timeline for baseline and extended bench.
[00:20] James Lee: Great, the main thing for us is fidelity to our production calls — we stream tokens back to our frontend for a chat UX, so streaming perf matters. We also have batch offline rerank jobs, non-streaming.
[00:33] Amir Khan: For infra, we care about steady state concurrency and cold start characteristics; we use a mix of short chat queries (50-120 tokens) and long summaries (800-2k tokens).
[00:45] Marco Ruiz: Nice, that's helpful. Two immediate mapping items: streaming vs non-streaming will change the harness config — streaming keeps the connection open and sends deltas, non-streaming is request/response. Also if you use chunked streaming (delayed partials) that's another mode.
[01:02] Olivia Chen: Can you confirm success criteria? Examples we usually see: p95 latency for streaming first-byte and end-to-end, p50/p95 token throughput, and cost-per-1M tokens. What should we focus on?
[01:14] Sarah Patel: p95 for time-to-first-token is critical for UX — target under 300ms mostly for short chats, for long summaries p95 end-to-end under 4s would be acceptable. Cost target is more flexible but want to understand cost at scale for 1M tokens and per-concurrent-user.
[01:30] Marco Ruiz: Ok we'll capture that. James, when you say streaming first-byte, do you want us to measure both first-byte latency and median byte-per-timestep?
[01:38] James Lee: Yes, both. Also measure model quality metrics — at least basic BLEU/ROUGE or similarity vs baseline model. We can provide a small eval set.
[01:49] Nina Park: We'll need your inference scripts — do you have a standardized client? We support python scripts and curl; harness can wrap them.
[01:56] James Lee: We have a python client built on aiohttp that streams chunks. We'll share repo link; expect it to be a bit messy.
[02:03] Amir Khan: We'll also give a sample S3 bucket with ~5k example sessions. Privacy note: nothing PII.
[02:08] Olivia Chen: Perfect. For the harness: Marco, quick high-level on how we integrate customer scripts.
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: Sure - Redwood's benchmark harness runs in a sandboxed EC2 container or k8s job. We can mount your script and dataset. The harness has drivers for streaming (we instrument the websocket or HTTP chunked responses) and non-streaming in parallel. We support varying concurrency with a loader process that can do ramp-up, steady-state, and ramp-down phases.
[02:34] Sarah Patel: How do you handle warm/cold starts? We need cold start percentiles, because we have autoscaling and sometimes pods are spun down.
[02:42] Marco Ruiz: We have a warm-up mode where we flush caches and then spawn new workers to measure cold start times; we also capture KV cache hit statistics where available, though not all open models expose that.
[02:53] James Lee: You mentioned KV cache — will that be representative with our sessions? Our sessions reuse prefixes a lot so cache helps a lot.
[02:59] Marco Ruiz: Right, we can emulate your prefix distribution; if you provide a trace we'll mirror the prefix reuse to approximate cache hit rates.
[03:09] Olivia Chen: Security — quick callout: Nimbus asked earlier about VPC/private deployments and KMS. For the pilot harness runs we can do hosted tests but if you need VPC we can run within a customer VPC in Redwood Private. Any constraints on data residency?
[03:23] Sarah Patel: For the POC it's fine to use hosted infra, but must use customer-managed KMS keys if we upload any encrypted sample data. For longer pilot we'll need VPC. SOC 2 and audit logs are required.
[03:33] Olivia Chen: Noted. We'll attach our SOC 2 doc and the runbook for running within a VPC.
[03:40] Amir Khan: For benchmarking, how do you vary quantization/profile? We want to test int8 and bf16 profiles we use in production too.
[03:48] Marco Ruiz: Harness supports multiple model variants and quant profiles. We'll run baseline full-precision then int8/QAT where applicable. For some models int8 can impact quality; we'll report delta against your eval set.
[04:01] James Lee: Regarding models — we'll test against the open model we currently use (r-w v2 13b? i think it's redwood-13b variant) but also want Redwood's recommended variant for lower latency.
[04:12] Marco Ruiz: We'll include Redwood-13B-int8 and r_w2-13b-fp16 comparators.
[04:18] Sarah Patel: On metrics, please capture p50/p95 token latency, time-to-first-token (streaming), end-to-end, throughput (tokens/sec), and cost-estimate per 1M tokens given the chosen config.
[04:29] Olivia Chen: We'll put together a default dashboard template for those metrics.
[04:33] James Lee: One thing — our app uses streaming with per-token suppression and stop sequences; that can change effective throughput. Can you run harness with the same decoding params?
[04:44] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can pass your decoding params into the harness; please include them in your script or a params.json.
[04:51] Amir Khan: For load shape — we anticipate 500 steady concurrent users at peak, average 300, with session token distribution skewed (70% short chats, 30% long). We'll upload telemetry to show distribution.
[05:02] Marco Ruiz: Good. For a baseline run we'll do a 15-minute ramp to steady-state, 30-minute steady-state, then 5-minute ramp down — that should match your production burst patterns.
[05:12] Olivia Chen: Timeline — propose: Olivia shares harness and runbook by Mon 3/23, Nimbus shares scripts and data by Wed 3/25. Marco runs baseline configs Wed-Fri 3/25-27 and we review results on Mon 3/29. Does that work?
[05:25] Sarah Patel: That timeline works for us.
[05:27] James Lee: Yes. Quick clarification: do you run streaming tests in real-time or as replay?
[05:33] Marco Ruiz: We can do both. Real-time streaming will open connections to the model and measure network+model latency. Replay mode simulates client timing but doesn't fully measure network jitter — we recommend real-time for first-byte metrics.
[05:46] Nina Park: Also to call out, sometimes transcription/autogen of measurement conflates first-byte with first-token; we'll label them separately in the dashboard.
[05:55] Amir Khan: For the pilot, do you provide the harness as code we can run in our own account? We prefer running in our account to validate VPC/KMS.
[06:03] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we have a self-hosted harness bundle that's been used by a few customers. We'll share an infra quickstart and a helm chart. For initial run Redwood can run it in our infra and then we can hand over to Nimbus for a run in your account.
[06:18] James Lee: Nice. On the quality side, we want side-by-side outputs for 200 eval prompts. We'll check ROUGE and some human spot checks.
[06:28] Olivia Chen: We'll include a seeded sampling run to produce deterministic outputs for comparisons.
[06:33] Sarah Patel: Any constraints on token limits or model context? We often hit 4096 for long docs, planning to move to 32k soon.
[06:42] Marco Ruiz: Context lengths are supported up to 128k depending on model; we'll test at 4k and 32k if you want. Note longer context impacts memory and throughput; we'll include that in the cost calc.
[06:56] James Lee: Regarding metrics export — CSV? grafana? Prometheus?
[07:01] Marco Ruiz: We export raw CSV and an automatically generated grafana/tempo dashboard for visualization. We'll also attach a spreadsheet with cost breakdowns.
[07:10] Olivia Chen: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners. Olivia to send harness link and our SOC 2 and runbook. Marco to prepare baseline configs including streaming and non-streaming, and default quant profiles. James to upload scripts and evaluation set. Amir to send concurrency telemetry. We schedule review 3/29.
[07:29] Sarah Patel: Sounds good. A couple of quick questions: do you simulate network latency for edge users? We have users in APAC with high RTTs.
[07:37] Marco Ruiz: We can add an artificial latency shim in the harness to emulate RTTs. We'll run regional tests too if you want.
[07:45] James Lee: Competitors — just so you know, we've been evaluating Anthropic for streaming and OpenAI for baseline quality. Cost and private deployment are big differentiators for Redwood.
[07:56] Olivia Chen: Understood. We'll make sure to call out dedicated vs hosted comparisons in the report, including Dedicated reserved capacity costs.
[08:05] Nina Park: Final note: please include your desired success criteria in the shared doc so we don't assume.
[08:10] Sarah Patel: We'll add concrete numbers to the doc tonight. Thanks all.
[08:14] Olivia Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and SOW draft.

-- End of transcript --
